faq.a: Hadil is associated with the Arabic form هديل, whose core sense is the cooing of a dove; melodious sound.

faq.q: What is the origin of Hadil?
faq.a: Hadil is associated with Arabic. Hadil is a transliteration of Arabic هديل (Hadīl) 'the cooing of a dove; a gentle melodious sound'. The source gloss 'delicate, tender, agile' is an extrapolation of the dove image rather than the lexical meaning; same word as hadeel.
Yes — the underlying form هديل is Arabic.
Hadil can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Hadil should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. False

faq.q: What does Hadil mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Hadil is rendered ہدیل and carries the sense کبوتر کی کوک، سریلی آواز.

faq.q: What does Hadil mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Hadil is rendered هدیل and carries the sense آواز کبوتر، نوای خوش.
A romanized syllable approximation is ha-dil. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Hadil?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Hadil, hadil. Script forms are هديل, هدیل, ہدیل, हदील.

faq.q: Is Hadil a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
